title: Dead field → link by co-occurrence, not by dead reference
trigger: A foreign key field exists but is never populated by the producer — don't fix the producer, link by shared scope instead.
principle: When a foreign key field is never set by the producer, linking by co-occurrence (same scope/context) is more robust than trying to fix the producer. All entities on the same page/tab/window belong to that scope's primary entity — use that implicit relationship instead of a dead reference.

cases.context: Subtitle detector never sets subtitle.videoId — all subtitles on a video page belong to that page's video but no explicit link exists
cases.bad:
// Wait for detector to set videoId — it never does
const video = videos.find(v => v.id === subtitle.videoId); // always undefined → no filename match

cases.context: Event correlation via correlationId that the producer never includes
cases.bad:
// Group events by correlationId — field is always null
const groups = events.filter(e => e.correlationId === target.correlationId); // empty groups
cases.good:
// Group by timestamp window within same request scope
const groups = events.filter(e => Math.abs(e.ts - target.ts) < WINDOW_MS && e.scope === target.scope);

applyFor: Orphaned foreign keys (field exists but never set by producer)
Event correlation (link events by timestamp window, not by correlationId if missing)
Log enrichment (link log lines by request scope, not by traceId if missing)
Any entity relationship where the linking field is unreliable or never populated
